newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Clipsal continues expansion, sees more JVs.
newsitem.headline: Clipsal continues expansion, sees more JVs.

text.p: Electrical fittings company Clipsal Industries Holdings Ltd was continuing to expand rapidly in Asia and expected to announce two new joint ventures in the next six months, senior officials said on Tuesday.
"We are expanding quite rapidly in almost every market in Asia, that includes Hongkong, China, Taiwan and also the whole of the ASEAN region," Clipsal chairman Victor Lo told a news briefing.
ASEAN is the Association of Southeast Asian Nations comprising Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, Brunei, the Philippines and Vietnam.
Clipsal has moved into new markets like Vietnam and India, where it is in the final stages of negotiating a joint venture.
The Indian joint venture was being handled by its Australian unit Gerard Industries and an agreement was expected in the next three months, Lo said.
In China, Clipsal is looking at extending its joint venture with General Electric, which produces circuit protection products.
"The products are mostly sold in China and when production is big enough we will expect to export to Asia with GE and Clipsal brands," Lo said.
In China, the products are sold under a joint GE-Clipsal brand.
Later on, Clipsal could extend the GE joint venture into other part of Asia, Lo said.
K.W. Chau, Clipsal's managing director, said the company was planning manufacturing facilities on a 100,000 sq m plot of land it had bought in Huizhou, China.
Clipsal can build 60,000 sq m of facilities and construction is expected to take place in the next 12 to 18 months.
The first phase of the facilities, which will be used to increase production capacity in China, is expected to be ready in 1999, Lo added.

The new facilities would also be used to make contactors -- an area in which Clipsal is also negotiating a joint venture with a European company. An agreement is expected in the next six months, Chau said.
Some US$4-5 million of funds from a recent placement exercise will finance the new China facilities, Lo said.
In Australia, where Clipsal already has 65 percent market share in electrical wiring accessories, it was broadening its products into circuit breakers and industrial switch gears.
Clipsal is supplying lighting products for the commercial market in Australia through Gerard Industries and has also taken up distribution in Hong Kong, Singapore and China, Lo said.

"The major decision is at what point in time will we make a major commitment into manufacturing these lighting products in Asia," Lo said, adding that it was a necessary step for Clipsal to become a major supplier of commercial lighting products.
Lighting products were bulky and expensive to transport and store and closeness to the markets was also important, he said.
Lo said Clipsal was working on manufacturing lighting products but was not ready to say when that would take place.

On Clipsal's growth prospects, Lo said: "Looking at the fundamentals in the mid- to long term, I don't see why the sort of growth rates we have been achieving in the last few years cannot be achieved in the next few years."
Clipsal recorded a 14.8 percent rise in net profit to Singapore $23.2 million on a turnover of S$178.9 million for the fiscal year ended December 31, 1996.
-- Singapore newsroom (65-8703080)
